AWAR D 1.
The present claim petition is filed by the petitioner for claiming compensation on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident which happened on 26.04.2018.

sentences.text: Brief facts as narrated in the present claim petition are that the accident in the present case took place on 26.04.2018.

It is the case of the petitioner that on 26.04.2018, petitioner Pawan Kumar was going to Bulandshahr with his elder brother and his nephew Vivek on the motorcycle bearing Registration No.UP-13AW-1354.
When they reached near Rahul Vihar, in the meantime, a roadways bus bearing Registration No.UP-17D-1062 being driven in rash and negligent manner, came from behind and hit them.
Due to the said incident, they received grievous injuries.
3. On notice of the petition, all the respondents have marked their appearance and filed their separate written statements.

3(i). Respondent no. 1 & 2 have filed their joint written statement wherein they stated that petitioner is not entitled for any compensation from the answering respondent as petitioner was triple riding on victim vehicle and overtaking the bus in a high speed and he was driving his motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner.

It is further submitted that at the time of accident, Respondent No.1 was having a valid driving licence to drive the commercial vehicle and the same is insured with New India Insurance Company Ltd.
3(ii).

In his separate written statement, respondent No.3/UPSRTC has contended that R2 is the owner of the alleged vehicle/bus bearing Registration No.UP-17D-1062, which was running on contract basis with UPSRTC.

As per the contract agreement, if any accident takes place, it would be liability of the owner of vehicle and insurance company of the bus as the bus is insured with the New India Assurance Company Ltd.
Other general defences have been taken by R3/UPSRTC.
4. Respondent no. 4 / insurance company has taken the general defences.

Further, it is stated that amount claimed as compensation by the claimant is highly exaggerated and exorbitant and is in no way tenable at all, keeping into consideration the absence of proof of age, occupation, status, income contributions etc.

Other general defences have been taken by R4/The New India Assurance Ltd.
5.

On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed on 03.03.2020:-
(i) Whether the petitioner Pawan Kumar suffered injuries in a motor vehicular accident, which happened on 26.04.018 at 09:00 A.M. near Rahul Vihar, NH-24,
Ghaziabad, U.P., within jurisdiction of PS Vijay Nagar, due to rash and negligent driving of bus bearing Regn. No. UP-17D-1062 driven by Respondent No.1/Dinesh Chand ( OPP)?
(ii) Whether petitioner is entitled to the compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP) 
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?
6. In order to establish his claim, petitioner Pawan Kumar has examined himself as PW-1 and deposed on the strength of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A and he has relied upon following documents:-

Pawan Kumar vs Dinesh Chand on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182005118/
2  Copy of medical bills and treatment record is Mark A.  Copy of Aadhar Card of petitioner Ex.PW1/1.  Certified copy of the criminal case record is Ex. PW1/2
Qualification certificate of the petitioner is Ex.PW1/3
Disability certificate of the petitioner is Ex. PW1/4  Driving licence of petitioner is Ex. PW1/5 PW1 was duly cross-examined by the learned counsel for Respondent Nos.1, 2 & 4.
7. PW2 Dr. Hemant Sharma produced the disability certificate issued by Board is Ex.PW2/A and deposed that petitioner was having 3% permanent physical disability in relation to left lower limb.
8. R3W1 has produced original contract dated 17.01.2017 and attested route permit Ex.R3W1/1 and Ex.R3W1/2 respectively.

He further brought authorization letter Ex.R3W1/3.
9.

I have heard Sh. Nakul Sharma, Ld. Counsel for petitioner ; Sh. R.P. Singh, Ld. Counsel for R-1 &
R2 ; and Sh.Pradeep Kumar Gupta, Ld. Counsel for R-3 / UPSRTC and perused the record.

10. The issues are decided as follows:-
ISSUE No.1 :-
11.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the 'preponderance of probabilities' which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further, in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
12. Now in this case, petitioner Pawan Kumar is the injured and witness of the accident.
In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-1.

Petitioner deposed on oath that on 26.04.2018, he was going on his motorcycle and when reached near Rahul Vihar, the offending bus hit him as well as pillion rider i.e. his elder brother and further that offending bus was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, without caring for traffic rules.

13. FIR was registered on the complaint of petitioner/injured and though there is a delay of about three days in lodging of FIR, it is seen that no question has been put to the petitioner in his cross-examination on the point of delay and no dispute has been raised regarding the occurrence of accident and involvement of offending vehicle in the same.
After investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the truck.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima-facie points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima-facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 M.V. Act.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

Pawan Kumar vs Dinesh Chand on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182005118/
3

entities.text: Pawan Kumar vs Dinesh Chand on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.

In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
15.
Respondent no.1 and 2 i.e. the driver and the owner of the offending vehicle did not led any evidence to prove anything contrary to the claim of the petitioner.

In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.

entities.text: Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even the insurance company has not led any evidence to disprove the claim of the petitioner.
No such suggestion was given to the petitioner that accident was not caused by R1.
PW1 has denied the suggestion that he was driving his motorcycle in a fast and negligent manner.

It is seen that while in his petition, petitioner has mentioned that he was going on his motorcycle alongwith his elder brother and nephew at the time of accident, in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A, he has mentioned that he was alongwith his elder brother on the motorcycle.

It is amusing to note that in his cross-examination, PW1 admitted the suggestion of Ld. Counsel for R1 &
R2 by deposing that "It is correct that at the time of accident, I was riding on bike alongwith my wife and my minor child aged about three years.
It is correct that I have not mention (sic) this fact in my evidence by way of affidavit."

This statement of petitioner is in sharp contrast to the claim petition and his examination-in-chief but these sole suggestions in itself do not, in my considered view, lead to any presumption regarding anything to disprove the claim of the petitioner.

No suggestion was given to the petitioner that there was any contributory negligence or that, in order to cover any lapse, he had concealed the presence of his wife and his minor child on the bike or that the version in examination-in-chief regarding his elder brother being pillion rider on his motorcycle is incorrect.

No such suggestion was given to the petitioner so as to indicate that there were five persons seated on the motorcycle, including elder brother of the petitioner, his nephew, wife and child and himself.

Plea has been taken in the written statement by respondent no. 1 & 2 that petitioner was triple riding but there is no such suggestion to indicate as to how the factum of triple riding led to the accident in question.

In the MLC of the petitioner, alleged history of fall from bike is mentioned but this observation on the MLC is not in direct conflict with the testimony of the petitioner, even though he has not stated anywhere that due to being hit by the truck, he had fallen down from the bike.

Hence,
there is no need at all to go into the aspect of contributory negligence, once no contributory negligence on the part of petitioner is alleged by the petitioner and no issue was framed in this regard.
Further, though suggestion was given to the petitioner that accident took place due to his fault, the same was denied by the petitioner.

Ld. Counsel for the insurer / R-3 also raised the plea that it was a case of triple riding, both as per FIR and testimony of the petitioner and hence contributory negligence can be inferred in this case.
However, I do not find merit in such a contention.
In Bimla Devi Vs. Surjeet Singh & Ors., P & H dated 08.04.2016, it was held that the factum of three persons riding on the motor-cycle is no ground to hold them contributory negligence.

entities.text: Bimla Devi Vs. Surjeet Singh & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case at hand, the petitioner was hit from behind and there is nothing to suggest that the triple riding was responsible for causing of the accident or that accident could have been averted if petitioner was not triple riding.
No such suggestion was put to PW1 to show that his hands and leg movement was restricted due to congestion on the victim vehicle and it led to petitioner loosing control over the vehicle.

sentences.text: Copy of MLC of the petitioner is not filed on record and there is nothing to suggest that any MLC was prepared.
Medical document of LBS Hospital are on record and shows that petitioner was admitted to hospital on 26.04.2018 with history of fall from bike.

It is not disputed that petitioner was travelling on a bike and none of the respondents have disputed the occurrence of the accident and involvement of offending bus, even though R1 & R2 have raised the plea of negligence on the part of petitioner.
There is no mechanical inspection report of offending bus placed on record by the petitioner and there is nothing to suggest that bus and victim motorcycle were subjected to mechanical inspection.

However, in my considered view, these inconsistencies do not throw away the claim of the petitioner as neither R3 & R4 alleged any collusion between petitioner on one side and R1 & R2 on the other side, nor it is stated in the written statement by R1 & R2 that accident did not take place with the offending bus in question.
No such suggestion was given to PW1 either by counsel for R1 & R2 or by Ld.
Counsel
for R4
that the offending bus is falsely implicated or was not present at the spot or was not involved in the accident.
Rather, suggestion has been given that accident was not caused due to rash and negligent driving of R1 and that it was caused due to negligent driving of petitioner himself.
The medical document of the petitioner dated 01.05.2018 of LBS Hospital reflects that it was a follow-up case of fracture malleolus fracture and calcane fracture.
Medical document also suggests that petitioner had suffered from injuries in left leg.
The disability certificate Ex.PW1/4 of the petitioner shows that petitioner was suffering from fracture malleolus and calcane in left lower limb.

17. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence and for filing of charge-sheet, it is proved that the petitioner Pawan Kumar received grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of Respondent No.1 Dinesh Chand, the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE No.2:-
18. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
19. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to Pawan Kumar vs Dinesh Chand on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182005118/
5 be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.

entities.text: Pawan Kumar vs Dinesh Chand on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.
20. Now, in the present case, injured Pawan Kumar has suffered grievous injuries.
Disability certificate was filed and relied on by the petitioner.

Therefore, on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to him under the aforesaid heads as follows :-
MEDICAL EXPENSES:
21.
Petitioner has not filed and proved on record a single medical bill.
The medical documents on record suggests that the entire treatment was in a government hospital and free of cost.
Hence, no amount is being given as compensation under this head.
MACP No. 156/18 Pawan Kumar Vs. Dinesh Chand & Ors. Page 10 of PAIN AND SUFFERING:

entities.text: MACP No. 156/18 Pawan Kumar Vs. Dinesh Chand & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 22. According to his affidavit, petitioner received grievous injuries in the accident and was admitted to LBS Hospital.
There is nothing to suggest that petitioner was admitted in the hospital as an impatient even for a single date and no discharge summary is filed on record.
However, the follow-up document of the same hospital reflects that petitioner suffered from fracture in left leg.
Petitioner stated in his testimony by way of affidavit attested on 07.06.2023 that his treatment was continuing but no document in proof of such a claim of his is filed on record.
The last document of LBS Hospital is of 01.05.2018.
Petitioner suffered from grievous injuries and hence, it is clear that petitioner must have remained under considerable pain.
Therefore, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.20,000/- to the petitioner under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 23.
The petitioner has not proved any actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.10,000/- to petitioner for conveyance and special diet charges.
24. Petitioner has claimed attendant expenses but no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment.

Considering the nature of injuries as reflected through the medical documents placed on record, there cannot be an inference that actual services of any family member were consistently required by the petitioner for any given period of time.
He sustained grievous injuries and hence it is quite possible that his family members might have rendered him some assistance.
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- as attendant charges.

Pawan Kumar vs Dinesh Chand on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182005118/
6 25.
Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.20,000/- (10,000+10,000) under this head.

LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :
26.

Petitioner has claimed that he was working as a fabricator and earning Rs. 15,000/- per month but disabled due to accident and loss of earning of 12 months and further that he has been disabled to do any work and cannot walk properly, driver and stand for long time.
Petitioner has not filed on record any document in proof of his employment/occupation and income.
He has not placed on record his bank statement to reflect that he consistently received any amount of income from his occupation.
He has not even disclosed the address of his place of work in his testimony.
Though, he disclosed in his cross-examination that he was working as a fabricator at Seemapuri, Delhi on daily wages but did not mention the address of his work place.
He admitted that he has not filed any income proof and bank statement and further that he does not have any Diploma Certificate regarding fabrication work.

Hence, the Tribunal is of the considered view that a balanced approach should be taken and as petitioner has claimed to be a fabricator by profession and has failed to prove his salary and educational qualification and skill but has proved on record his intermediate marksheet Ex.PW1/3 which shows that he had studied upto 12th class, his salary is estimated as per the minimum wages applicable to a skilled worker in Uttar Pradesh at the time of accident, as petitioner is stated to be a resident of Uttar Pradesh.

Though, petitioner claimed that he MACP No.
156/18 Pawan Kumar Vs. Dinesh Chand & Ors. Page 12 of was working in Seemapuri, Delhi, no proof of his residence in Delhi or daily commute from Bulandshahr, U.P. to Delhi is filed and proved on record.

MACP No.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The driving licence and Aadhar Card of petitioner Ex.PW1/5 also reflects his address as that of Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh.

In view of the same, income of the petitioner has to be calculated as per the minimum wages applicable in the state of UP under the category skilled worker at the time of accident, which is Rs.9,381/- per month.

Considering the nature of injuries being grievous, the period and course of treatment and keeping in mind the nature of job of the petitioner,
it is not difficult to presume that in case of fracture and injuries sustained as above-mentioned,
Petitioner
must have been disabled from work for about two months as this would have been the minimum time to heal.
Therefore, I award Rs.18,762/- (9381x2) as compensation under this head.
Therefore, his loss of income for two months is calculated as Rs.18,762/-.
LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY.
27. The next question that remains to be decided is the compensation with respect to the disability of the petitioner.
Under this head, it has to be seen that what could be the future loss of income on account of disability.

The disability certificate of Dr. Hedgewar Arogya Sansthan clearly shows that the petitioner is the case of 3% disability as it was a follow-up case of fracture malleolus fracture and calcane fracture.
PW2 Dr. Hemant Sharma has been examined as an expert witness on disability certificate issued by the Disability Board.

According to the disability certificate Ex.PW2/A,
petitioner suffered 3% permanent disability.
Further, PW2 admitted in his cross-examination that the disability was unlikely to affect activity of daily living.
The petitioner has MACP No. 156/18 Pawan Kumar Vs. Dinesh Chand & Ors.

sentences.text: Page 13 of not narrated how this disability will come in way of reducing the efficiency of the work in which the petitioner is engaged.

There is nothing brought Pawan Kumar vs Dinesh Chand on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182005118/
7 on record by petitioner to suggest that he was unable to work after the accident.
He has not proved that due to this injury, his income has reduced.
Petitioner has not explained as to in what manner he will not be able to work as per his ability and qualification.

Petitioner has not led any evidence to show what work he was doing prior to accident and what work is being done by him in the office post accident, to arrive at any conclusion that petitioner's nature of job has changed drastically to his detriment and that it is due to accident solely.
It is not the plea of the petitioner that he has suffered from any loss of income on account of accident.
Rather, petitioner has not even led any cogent evidence to prove his occupation and income.
In case titled as Ramvir Singh Vs. Rajesh Kumar & Ors.

In case bearing citation Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Arising out of civil appeal No. 8918 of 2010, it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that :-
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claim could carry on inspite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether ; (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether inspite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and MACP No. 156/18 Pawan Kumar Vs. Dinesh Chand & Ors. Page 14 of functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.

entities.text: Pawan Kumar Vs. Dinesh Chand & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For example, if the left hand of the claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or disablement may be around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver of a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be 100%, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant is clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could performed his clerical functions, in that even the loss of earnings capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter nor 60% which is the actual physical disability but far less.

In fact, there may not be need to award any compensation under the head of 'Loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in Government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities on the consequences of losing his hand....."
Hence, functional disability of petitioner is taken to be Zero % and no amount is being given under this head.

INTEREST 29.
Petitioner has pursued his case since year 2018.
Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

LIABILITY:
30.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.
During cross-examination of R3W1, it was suggested to him that offending vehicle did not have a valid route permit, which was denied by him.
No issue was framed regarding violation of route permit and no evidence was led by R4 in this regard.

Rather, R3/UPSRTC as examined R3W1,
who deposed about the general route permit and proved on record the contract with the owner of the offending vehicle and R3/UPSRTC.

Even though the bus number is not specified in the general order w.r.t the route permit, Ld. Counsel for R3 argued that the order is still in force and further the number of vehicles on the said route from Bulandshahr to Kaushambi remain 40 as per the limit provided in the said order but different vehicles keep on being hired on contract for plying on the said route and the copy of the order of Regional Manager, Ghaziabad, UPSRTC reflects that on the date of accident, the vehicle of R2 bearing No. UP-17D-1062 was one of those 40 vehicles plying on the said route.
I find merit in the submission of Ld. Counsel for R3/UPSRTC.

Hence, I do not find it to be a case of route violation, particularly when nothing could be extracted during the cross-examination of R3W1 by R4 in this regard and no evidence in support of any breach of MACP No. 156/18 Pawan Kumar Vs. Dinesh Chand & Ors.

entities.text: MACP No. 156/18 Pawan Kumar Vs. Dinesh Chand & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Page 16 of insurance policy was led by Insurance Company and no evidence was led by R4/Insurance Company to show that there was any route permit violation by R3, R1 & R2.
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured, the Insurance company is liable to compensate the third party.
In view of above, it is held that respondent no.4/ insurer shall be liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

RELIEF:
31.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.59,000/- (Rupees Fifty Nine Thousand Only) along with interest @ 7.5% per Pawan Kumar vs Dinesh Chand on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182005118/
9 annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization in favour of petitioner against the Respondent No.4/ The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.

opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed on 03.03.2020:-
(i) Whether the petitioner Pawan Kumar suffered injuries in a motor vehicular accident, which happened on 26.04.018 at 09:00 A.M. near Rahul Vihar, NH-24,
Ghaziabad, U.P., within jurisdiction of PS Vijay Nagar, due to rash and negligent driving of bus bearing Regn. No. UP-17D-1062 driven by Respondent No.1/Dinesh Chand ( OPP)?
(ii) Whether petitioner is entitled to the compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?
(OPP) 
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?
The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claim could carry on inspite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The third step is to find out whether ; (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether inspite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and MACP No. 156/18 Pawan Kumar Vs. Dinesh Chand & Ors. Page 14 of functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima-facie points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).
14. In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima-facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 M.V. Act.
If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.
Pawan Kumar vs Dinesh Chand on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182005118/
3
If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
15.
In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.
In the MLC of the petitioner, alleged history of fall from bike is mentioned but this observation on the MLC is not in direct conflict with the testimony of the petitioner, even though he has not stated anywhere that due to being hit by the truck, he had fallen down from the bike.
Hence,
there is no need at all to go into the aspect of contributory negligence, once no contributory negligence on the part of petitioner is alleged by the petitioner and no issue was framed in this regard.
In Bimla Devi Vs. Surjeet Singh & Ors., P & H dated 08.04.2016, it was held that the factum of three persons riding on the motor-cycle is no ground to hold them contributory negligence.
Pawan Kumar vs Dinesh Chand on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182005118/
4 16.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.
20. Now, in the present case, injured Pawan Kumar has suffered grievous injuries.
Hence, the Tribunal is of the considered view that a balanced approach should be taken and as petitioner has claimed to be a fabricator by profession and has failed to prove his salary and educational qualification and skill but has proved on record his intermediate marksheet Ex.PW1/3 which shows that he had studied upto 12th class, his salary is estimated as per the minimum wages applicable to a skilled worker in Uttar Pradesh at the time of accident, as petitioner is stated to be a resident of Uttar Pradesh.
In view of the same, income of the petitioner has to be calculated as per the minimum wages applicable in the state of UP under the category skilled worker at the time of accident, which is Rs.9,381/- per month.
Considering the nature of injuries being grievous, the period and course of treatment and keeping in mind the nature of job of the petitioner,
it is not difficult to presume that in case of fracture and injuries sustained as above-mentioned,
The petitioner has MACP No. 156/18 Pawan Kumar Vs. Dinesh Chand & Ors.
He has not proved that due to this injury, his income has reduced.
Petitioner has not led any evidence to show what work he was doing prior to accident and what work is being done by him in the office post accident, to arrive at any conclusion that petitioner's nature of job has changed drastically to his detriment and that it is due to accident solely.
It is not the plea of the petitioner that he has suffered from any loss of income on account of accident.
